editorial:
Ever feel like you are just invisible in your own home? That is exactly where Lizzie and Sarah find themselves. They are two middle-aged suburban wives who spend their days being ignored or put down by their selfish husbands. Their only escape is a local amateur acting group where they can finally feel important. The movie starts with a heavy mood after a local teen dies in a freak accident, but it quickly turns into a wild ride. After a truly terrible birthday lunch, these two friends decide they have had enough. They head out for a shopping trip that turns into a chaotic plan for revenge, and it is surprisingly satisfying to watch them snap.

The acting is the best part here because you really feel for these women before they start causing trouble. The pacing is steady, though some parts of the drama feel a bit slow until the revenge kicks in. If you enjoy dark comedies about ordinary people hitting their breaking point, you will love this. Since it is an older TV movie, you might not find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but it is definitely worth renting on Apple TV for a cozy night in. Adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great shout if you like quirky British humor.
endingExplained: After their wild day of rebellion, the women finally stand up to their husbands in a big way. They use the skills they learned from their acting club to manipulate the situation and get the upper hand. Instead of going back to their boring, sad lives, they choose their own happiness and friendship over their toxic marriages. They end up free from the emotional weight of their husbands, proving that it is never too late to start over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about underdogs getting revenge.
